issues.description: Tests fabricate a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash Addition to satisfy CreateSignedTransaction's non-empty additions invariant
issues.detail: Tests changed `additions=[]` to `additions=[Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]` purely to get past `__post_init__`'s `len(additions) < 1` guard while real outputs come from cat_discrepancy. This is a sentinel value standing in for absence — a clear LSP/contract violation. Either relax the precondition when cat_discrepancy is present, or model absence honestly.

issues.description: send_transaction silently changes puzzle_decorator semantics from `[0]`-only slicing to forwarding the whole list
issues.detail: The old code passed `[request.puzzle_decorator[0].to_json_dict()]` — exactly one decorator. The new path forwards the entire list to CreateSignedTransaction, while cat_spend drops puzzle_decorator entirely. Two endpoints, two divergent silent semantic changes. Pick one contract and document it.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction complects three distinct request shapes by absorbing CAT and decorator fields
issues.detail: Adding extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator onto a general transaction type collapses XCH-send, CAT-spend, and signed-tx-creation into one record with unstated valid field combinations. No __post_init__ check guards mutually exclusive combinations. Define a small CatDiscrepancy value type and keep request shapes honest.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation duplicates the tri-state invariant across two dataclasses instead of owning it once
issues.detail: Both CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction carry the same three Optional fields and the same forwarding property. The validation belongs to a CatDiscrepancy ADT constructed once at the boundary; as written, the two classes are kept in sync by convention and a future field rename will silently break one. The extracted free function captures behavior but not the type.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation preserves opaque `None in {set}` membership and type: ignore comments instead of clean narrowing
issues.detail: The helper is moved verbatim with three `# type: ignore[arg-type]` and a set-membership trick whose correctness depends on hashing semantics of mixed bytes/str/None. An explicit `any(x is None for x in (...))` or a TypeGuard would narrow properly and delete the ignores. Extracting bad taste into a function makes it reusable, not better.

issues.description: get_wallet called purely for its raising side effect with `# opportunity to raise` is a smuggled assertion
issues.detail: The discarded call hides intent behind a comment, and create_signed_transaction will redo the same lookup. Extract a named `validate_wallet_type(id, Wallet)` helper so the precondition is structural, not folkloric. The current shape will confuse the next reader and is duplicated at two call sites.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the deduplication instinct is right but the execution leaks. The loudest signal — flagged by all six reviewers — is that tests had to fabricate a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash Addition to satisfy CreateSignedTransaction's non-empty-additions invariant, indicating the data model does not fit the wrapped call. Two silent behavior changes were also caught: send_transaction now forwards the whole puzzle_decorator list instead of just `[0]`, while cat_spend drops it entirely. The widened CreateSignedTransaction complects three request shapes, the moved cat_discrepancy_validation preserves its opaque set-membership check and type: ignores, and `get_wallet` calls survive only for side-effect raising. Fix the additions contract, capture the CAT discrepancy as its own ADT, and pin down the semantic changes before merge.
